examples.en: I'm making a travel plan for this vacation.
I made a study plan before the exam.

examples.ko: 계획을 세우면 시간을 아낄 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you make a plan, you can save time.

examples.ko: 주말마다 가족과 함께 계획을 세우는 게 즐거워요.
examples.en: It's fun to make plans with my family every weekend.

examples.ko: 먼저 예산을 보고 계획을 세워 보세요.
examples.en: First look at the budget and then try to make a plan.
We made a plan, but it rained so we canceled.

explain: '계획을 짜다'도 아주 자주 쓰는데, 일정이나 순서를 구체적으로 만들 때 특히 잘 어울려요. '계획을 세우다'는 큰 방향을 정하는 느낌까지 넓게 쓸 수 있어요. 반대 상황은 '계획이 틀어지다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.example: 친구와 함께 주말 여행 계획을 짜요.
phrases.en: I'm making a weekend trip plan with my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '계획을 세우다'와 비슷하지만 일정과 순서를 구체적으로 만들 때 더 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '계획을 세우다', but it fits better when you work out a detailed schedule and order.

phrases.en: Do you have any plans tomorrow?
phrases.nuance_ko: 계획을 이미 정했는지 물을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to ask or say whether you already have plans.

phrases.en: It rained, so I changed my travel plan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세운 계획을 다르게 고칠 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when you change a plan you already made.

explain_en: '계획을 짜다' is also very common and fits especially well when you build a concrete schedule or order of steps. '계획을 세우다' can cover the broader sense of setting a direction. The opposite situation is described with '계획이 틀어지다'.

examples.en: I have to make a decision by the end of this week.
We make important decisions together with the team members.
If you don't decide quickly, you'll miss the chance.

examples.ko: 저는 혼자 의사결정하는 게 아직 어려워요.
examples.en: It is still hard for me to make decisions alone.
Please explain how you made the decision.
If you decide based on data, you make fewer mistakes.

explain: '결정하다'가 더 일반적인 말이고, '의사결정하다'는 회사나 회의처럼 조직에서 방향을 정할 때 잘 어울려요. 명사 '의사결정', '의사결정권'도 같이 알아 두면 좋아요.

phrases.en: We have to decide by the end of today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 더 쉽고 넓게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler word with a wider range in everyday life.

phrases.en: We finally reached a conclusion at the meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 토론이나 고민 끝에 답을 정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when settling on an answer after discussion or thought.

phrases.example: 그 일은 팀장님이 의사결정권을 갖고 있어요.
phrases.en: The team leader has the authority to decide that matter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결정할 수 있는 권한을 가리키는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun referring to the authority to make decisions.

explain_en: '결정하다' is the more general word, while '의사결정하다' fits when an organization, such as a company or a meeting, sets a direction. It is also useful to learn the nouns '의사결정' and '의사결정권' (decision-making authority).

examples.en: On Lunar New Year, I send messages to all my friends.

examples.ko: 모임 장소가 바뀌어서 회원들에게 연락을 돌렸어요.
examples.en: The meeting place changed, so I contacted all the members.

examples.ko: 내일 행사가 취소돼서 모두에게 연락을 돌려야 해요.
examples.en: Tomorrow's event is canceled, so I have to contact everyone.

examples.ko: 반장이 반 친구들에게 연락을 돌리는 중이에요.
examples.en: The class president is contacting the classmates one by one.

examples.ko: 총무가 연락을 돌려서 열 명이 모였어요.
examples.en: The organizer contacted people, and ten gathered.

examples.ko: 동창 모임이 있다고 제가 먼저 연락을 돌릴게요.
examples.en: I'll let everyone know first that there's an alumni gathering.

explain: 같은 소식을 여러 사람에게 차례로 알릴 때 써요. 한 사람에게 연락하는 것은 '연락하다'라고 하니까 '돌리다'는 여러 명을 대상으로 할 때 어울려요. 단체 문자를 보내거나 한 명씩 전화하는 경우에 모두 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 모임 날짜가 바뀌어서 한 명씩 전화를 돌렸어요.
phrases.en: The meeting date changed, so I called everyone one by one.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 사람에게 차례로 전화로 알릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you phone many people in turn to tell them something.

phrases.en: I sent a group text to my classmates.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문자 하나로 여러 사람에게 한꺼번에 알릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you tell many people at once with one text.

phrases.en: I told my friends the news about my move.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소식이나 이야기를 알려 준다는 넓은 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broad phrase for passing news along to others.

explain_en: Use it when you pass the same news to many people one after another. Contacting one person is just '연락하다', so '돌리다' suits a group. It covers both sending a group text and phoning people one by one.

examples.en: My skills are gradually improving.
I heard the company plans to raise prices gradually.
If you increase your exercise gradually, you won't get hurt.
The patient's condition is improving steadily.
The new system will change step by step.
This work has to be carried out step by step.

explain: 변화가 한꺼번에 일어나지 않고 차례차례 조금씩 진행될 때 써요. 뉴스, 보고서, 공부 글에서 자주 보이고, 일상 대화에서는 '조금씩', '차근차근'이 더 편해요. 반대는 '급진적으로'나 '급격하게'예요.

phrases.en: The weather is getting warmer little by little.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대화에서 가장 편하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural choice in everyday conversation.

phrases.en: I'm carrying out the plan step by step.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서두르지 않고 순서대로 한다는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Suggests doing things in order without rushing.

phrases.en: My Korean is getting better and better.
phrases.nuance_ko: 변화가 계속 커지거나 작아질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a change keeps growing or shrinking.

explain_en: Use it when change happens little by little in order rather than all at once. It appears often in news, reports and study texts, while in daily talk '조금씩' or '차근차근' feel more natural. The opposite is '급진적으로' or '급격하게'.

en: to the maximum, as much as possible

examples.ko: 휴대폰 밝기를 최대로 올려도 햇빛 아래에서는 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: Even with the phone brightness at maximum, I can't see well in sunlight.
If you turn the volume up to the max, the neighbors will hear it.
I'm studying while making the most of my time.

examples.ko: 여행 가방에 짐을 최대로 넣었어요. 이제 더 안 들어가요.
examples.en: I packed the suitcase as full as it can go. Nothing more will fit now.

examples.ko: 에어컨을 최대로 틀어도 방이 안 시원해요.
examples.en: Even with the air conditioner at full, the room isn't cool.
I used all my strength and ran to the end.

explain: '최대한 빨리'의 '최대한'은 가능한 만큼 애쓴다는 말이고, '최대로'는 소리·밝기·온도처럼 단계가 있는 값을 맨 위에 맞출 때 잘 어울려요. '최대 다섯 명'처럼 '최대'만 쓰면 많아야 그 정도라는 한계를 나타내요. 반대는 '최소로'예요.

phrases.en: I'll come as fast as I can.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가능한 만큼 애쓴다는 뜻이라서 '빨리', '많이' 같은 말 앞에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means as much as possible, used before words like 'quickly' or 'a lot'.

phrases.example: 이 방에는 최대 열 명까지 들어갈 수 있어요.
phrases.en: This room can hold ten people at most.
phrases.nuance_ko: 많아야 그 정도라는 한계를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It states the upper limit, meaning no more than that.

phrases.en: I turned the volume up as high as it goes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '최대로'보다 쉬운 말이고, 소리나 크기에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler way to say it, used for volume or size.

explain_en: '최대한' in '최대한 빨리' stresses doing as much as one can, while '최대로' fits values with levels, such as volume, brightness, or temperature, set to the top. '최대' alone, as in '최대 다섯 명', marks an upper limit. The opposite is '최소로'.

en: to overdo it; to go too far

examples.ko: 친구 생일 선물을 너무 오버해서 샀어요.
examples.en: I overdid it buying my friend's birthday present.

examples.ko: 그 정도로 오버하지 마세요. 별일 아니에요.
examples.en: Don't go overboard. It's no big deal.

examples.ko: 동생이 또 오버해서 말했어요. 사실은 안 그랬어요.
examples.en: My younger brother exaggerated again. It wasn't really like that.

examples.ko: 처음 만났는데 너무 오버하는 거 아니에요?
examples.en: We just met, aren't you going a bit too far?

examples.ko: 운동할 때 오버하면 다음 날 몸이 아파요.
examples.en: If you overdo it when you exercise, your body hurts the next day.
Let's not overdo it today and take it slowly.

explain: 말, 행동, 반응이 지나칠 때 친구 사이에서 편하게 쓰는 구어예요. 조금 놀리거나 말리는 느낌이 있어서 '너무 오버하지 마'처럼 많이 말해요. 격식 있는 자리에서는 '지나치다', '과하다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: Don't overdo it. It's no big deal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구 사이에서 말릴 때 쓰는 반말이에요. 존댓말은 '오버하지 마세요'예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual way to tell a friend to stop going too far. The polite form adds the polite ending.

phrases.en: That joke went a little too far.
phrases.nuance_ko: '오버하다'보다 점잖은 말이라 조금 격식 있는 자리에서도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more proper word than the slangy one, so it also works in somewhat formal settings.

phrases.en: I think the gift is a bit too much.
phrases.nuance_ko: 양이나 정도가 넘칠 때 써요. 말이나 행동뿐 아니라 물건에도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the amount or degree is too much; it can describe things as well as words and actions.

explain_en: This is a casual spoken word for when someone's words, actions or reactions are too much. It often carries a teasing or cautioning tone, as in '너무 오버하지 마'. In formal settings, '지나치다' or '과하다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: This coffee shop gives you water for free.
I give my younger sibling pocket money.
My friend gave me a present.
The staff member gave me a receipt.

examples.ko: 저는 매일 아침 고양이한테 밥을 줘요.
examples.en: I feed my cat every morning.

explain: 어른에게 줄 때는 '드리다'를 써요. 선생님께 선물을 드려요. '주세요'는 내가 받고 싶을 때 써요.

phrases.en: to give someone a meaningful look (a silent hint)
phrases.nuance_ko: 말없이 표정이나 몸짓으로 알려 주다
phrases.nuance_en: giving a hint with a look or gesture, without words
phrases.en_equiv: to give someone a meaningful look (a silent hint)

dict_examples.ko: 생일을 맞은 동생에게 선물로 장난감을 주었다.
dict_examples.en: I gave a toy as a gift to my younger sibling on their birthday.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: When you give something to an older person, use 드리다: 선생님께 선물을 드려요. 주세요 is what you say when you want to receive something.

p.n: 내주다 stresses handing out something you were holding.

examples.ko: 어떤 대학에 갈지 아직 결정하지 못했어요.
examples.en: I haven't decided yet which university to go to.

examples.ko: 우리 어디서 만날지 지금 같이 결정해요.
examples.en: Let's decide together right now where to meet.
We'll wait. Take your time deciding on the menu.
That person will make the final decision.

examples.ko: 저는 옷을 살 때 뭘 살지 결정하기가 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard for me to decide what to buy when I shop for clothes.
After talking with my parents, I decided to move.

explain: '정하다'가 더 쉽고 일상적이라서 '메뉴를 정해요'처럼 가볍게 말해요. '결정하다'는 고민해서 마지막으로 고를 때 어울려요. '결정을 내리다'라는 말도 자주 써요. 저절로 정해지는 건 '결정되다'예요.

phrases.en: Let's pick the dinner menu.
phrases.nuance_ko: '결정하다'보다 쉽고 가벼워서 일상 대화에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier and lighter than 결정하다, common in daily talk.

phrases.en: After thinking for a long time, I made a decision.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고민한 끝에 마지막으로 정할 때 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used when you finally decide after much thought.

phrases.en: Both are good, so it is hard to decide.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-기 어렵다'를 붙여서 고르기 힘들다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -기 어렵다 says it is hard to choose.

explain_en: '정하다' is easier and more casual ('메뉴를 정해요'); '결정하다' fits a final choice made after some thought. '결정을 내리다' (make a decision) is also very common. When something just gets settled without you choosing, use the passive '결정되다'.

p.n: 정하다 is plainer and more everyday; 결정하다 sounds a bit weightier.

examples.en: I'm on the phone now.
Just a moment, I'm on a call.
I call the bank in the afternoon.
What are you doing now? — I'm on the phone with my mom.

examples.ko: 동생은 친구하고 한 시간 동안 전화해요.
examples.en: My younger sibling talks on the phone with a friend for an hour.

explain: 전화하다는 전화를 걸어서 말하는 거예요. 장소에는 “에”를 써요: 은행에 전화해요. 전화를 받는 것은 “전화를 받다”예요.

dict_examples.en: He phoned his wife and decided on a place to meet.

dict_examples.en: The two would call each other from time to time to ask how things were.

explain_en: 전화하다 means to call/phone someone. For an organization use 에: 은행에 전화해요. Answering the phone is 전화를 받다.

examples.en: In Korean writing class, I learned how to summarize.

examples.ko: 작문 숙제로 '내가 좋아하는 계절'에 대해 한 쪽을 써야 해요.
examples.en: For my writing homework I have to write one page about 'my favorite season'.

examples.ko: 작문을 잘하려면 먼저 많이 읽어야 해요.
examples.en: To be good at writing, you first have to read a lot.

examples.ko: 작문 시간에 친구들 앞에서 제 글을 읽었는데 너무 떨렸어요.
examples.en: In writing class I read my piece in front of my classmates, and I was so nervous.

examples.ko: 쓰기 시험에서는 작문 점수가 제일 낮았어요.
examples.en: On the writing test, my composition score was the lowest.

explain: '작문'은 학교나 시험에서 글쓰기를 연습하는 활동이에요. 일상에서 글을 쓴다고 말할 때는 '글쓰기'나 그냥 '쓰다'를 더 많이 써요.

dict_examples.en: To write a composition.

dict_examples.ko: 짝이 이번에 제출한 작문은 소설을 베낀 것이었다.
dict_examples.en: The composition my desk-mate submitted this time was copied from a novel.

dict_examples.ko: ‘나의 장래’라는 제목의 작문을 보고 나서 나를 불러 세운 것이다.
dict_examples.en: After looking at the composition titled 'My Future,' he called me over.

explain_en: '작문' is writing practice at school or on tests. In everyday talk, people say '글쓰기' or just '쓰다' for writing.

en: to hug, to hold in one's arms

examples.en: Mom is holding the baby.
We hadn't seen each other in ages, so I hugged my friend tight.

examples.ko: 친구가 울어서 제가 꼭 안아 줬어요.
examples.en: My friend was crying, so I gave them a tight hug.
The child plays holding a puppy in their arms.
I carried a big box in my arms up the stairs.

explain: 안다는 사람뿐 아니라 꽃이나 상자 같은 물건에도 써요. 글자는 '안다'이지만 [안따]라고 읽어요.
